Academics

Degree programs & pathways

From a foundational BA in Earth Sciences to fully funded PhD positions, the department offers eleven distinct degree pathways and seven minors and certificates. All require a substantive research or field component.

Bachelor's degrees

Undergraduate

Our four bachelor's programs share a common first-year foundation (the EAMS 1000-level sequence) before diverging into concentrations. Majors declare at the end of sophomore year and complete a senior capstone — either a research thesis or, for many Earth Sciences students, the four-week summer field camp at the Brennan Geological Reserve in central Maine.

Majors4
Total students287
Avg class size17
DeclarationEnd of Soph.

BA in Earth Sciences BA · 120 credits

The flagship undergraduate degree of the department since 1947. Field-intensive, with three required outdoor courses and a senior summer field-camp capstone. Concentrations let students specialize without losing breadth.

Concentrations (choose one)

  • Geology & Tectonics — classical hard-rock training for graduate study or industry
  • Surface Processes & Geomorphology — rivers, soils, glacial geology, coastal change
  • Earth Materials & Resources — mineralogy, petrology, economic geology
  • Paleobiology & Earth History — fossil record, deep-time climate, stratigraphy

Required core (all concentrations)

  • EAMS 1010 Dynamic Earth (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 1020 History of Life and Earth (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2110 Mineralogy (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2120 Optical Mineralogy & Petrology (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 3110 Structural Geology (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 3120 Sedimentology & Stratigraphy (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 4910 Summer Field Camp (6 cr., capstone)

Capstone

All students complete EAMS 4910 Summer Field Camp (4 weeks at the Brennan Geological Reserve, central Maine) or, with advisor approval, the two-semester EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis.

Declaration

Students typically declare the BA in Earth Sciences at the end of sophomore year. The declaration form (PDF) is available from Lecturer Park (M-202) and requires advisor signature plus completion of EAMS 1010 and 1020 with a grade of C or better.

BS in Atmospheric Sciences BS · 124 credits

A quantitative BS with a stronger physics/math core than the BA. Designed for students aiming at graduate study in atmospheric or climate sciences, or for entry to NOAA, NWS, or private-sector forecasting and consulting.

Concentrations

  • Weather & Forecasting — synoptic and mesoscale meteorology, operational forecasting practicum
  • Atmospheric Chemistry & Air Quality — chemistry-focused, with required laboratory rotation
  • Climate Dynamics — modeling-heavy, joint with the climate concentration of the MS track

Required core

  • EAMS 1110 Weather and Climate (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2410 Atmospheric Thermodynamics (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2420 Atmospheric Dynamics I (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 3410 Atmospheric Dynamics II (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 3420 Synoptic Meteorology (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2415 Forecasting Practicum (2 cr., taken twice)
  • EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis (6 cr., capstone)

Capstone

Two semesters of EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis with a faculty advisor, culminating in a public defense in late April. Recent theses have ranged from a re-analysis of the 2018 Northeast cold snap to a CIMS-based investigation of nighttime oxidation chemistry.

BS in Marine Sciences BS · 124 credits

A laboratory-and-field-intensive BS based at both Mendel Hall and the Cobbett Marine Laboratory (a 25-minute department shuttle ride from main campus). All Marine Sciences majors complete at least one cruise on the R/V Cobbett Bay.

Concentrations

  • Biological Oceanography & Marine Ecology
  • Chemical Oceanography & Marine Geochemistry
  • Physical Oceanography
  • Coastal & Estuarine Science

Required core

  • EAMS 1210 The Marine Environment (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2210 Coastal Sedimentary Systems (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2310 Biological Oceanography (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2320 Chemical Oceanography (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 2330 Physical Oceanography (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 3220 Sea-going Methods (4 cr.; includes 5-day cruise)
  • EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis (6 cr., capstone)

Capstone

Two semesters of EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis. Most theses involve at least one independent cruise day on the R/V Cobbett Bay, arranged through senior research scientist Reginald Greene.

BA in Environmental Studies (joint) BA · 120 credits

A joint degree with the Department of Public Policy. Designed for students who want a serious natural-science core paired with social science, policy, and ethics. Co-coordinated by Lecturer Ben-Ari (EAMS) and Prof. Goldfarb (Public Policy).

Concentrations

  • Environment & Society (policy-leaning)
  • Conservation Science (ecology-leaning)
  • Coastal & Watershed Management

Required core

  • EAMS 1310 Environment & Society (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 1010 Dynamic Earth or EAMS 1210 The Marine Environment
  • EAMS 1110 Weather and Climate
  • PUBP 2110 Foundations of Environmental Policy
  • PUBP 3220 Environmental Law
  • EAMS 3310 Climate Change Science & Policy (4 cr.)
  • EAMS 4990 Senior Research Thesis or PUBP 4990 Senior Policy Project

Declaration: Students may declare the joint major any time after completing EAMS 1310 and PUBP 2110.

Graduate — master's

Master's degrees

The department offers research master's (MS / MA, both thesis and non-thesis tracks) in each of the three core areas, plus a one-year Professional Master's in Environmental Data Science. Most research master's students are funded as part of an admitted PhD cohort and earn their MS en route to the doctorate.

MA / MS in Earth, Atmospheric, or Marine Sciences MA / MS · 32–36 credits

The standard research master's. Identical structure across the three areas; the difference between the MA and MS is a foreign-language requirement (MA) versus an additional quantitative methods sequence (MS).

Credits32–36
Typical duration2 years
FundedPhD-track
Cohort size~12 / yr

Thesis vs. non-thesis tracks

Thesis track (default)

Three-chapter research thesis defended in a public seminar, plus an oral exam by the thesis committee. Six credits of EAMS 5990. Standard for students continuing to the PhD.

Total: 32 credits.

Non-thesis track

Two additional graduate seminars and a written comprehensive exam in place of the thesis. Most often used by mid-career professionals or by PhD students who depart the program after coursework.

Total: 36 credits.

Professional MS in Environmental Data Science MS · 30 credits

A one-year (three-semester, including summer) terminal professional degree. Combines an Earth-systems foundation with a heavy data-science core. Designed for working professionals and recent science graduates moving into environmental analytics, climate-risk consulting, or government data science roles. Directed by Prof. Novak.

Credits30
Duration12 months
Tuition$48,200
Cohort cap22

Required courses

  • EAMS 5510 Reproducible Geoscience Computing (3 cr.)
  • EAMS 5520 Geospatial Analysis with R & Python (3 cr.)
  • EAMS 5530 Machine Learning for Earth Science (3 cr.)
  • EAMS 5310 Climate Dynamics (3 cr.)
  • EAMS 5410 Data Assimilation (3 cr.)
  • EAMS 5980 Applied Capstone (6 cr., paired with an external partner)
  • 9 additional credits of approved electives

Summer capstone partners (recent)

Massachusetts Coastal Zone Management, NOAA Northeast Fisheries, Climate Central, the Town of Brennan Resilience Office, and AECOM's regional climate-risk practice.

Graduate — doctoral

Doctor of Philosophy

EAMS admits roughly 10–14 PhD students per year across the three areas. All admitted students receive a five-year funding guarantee that covers full tuition, health insurance, and a 12-month stipend ($42,000 in AY 2025–26). Funding is provided through a combination of departmental fellowships, teaching assistantships, and external grants.

Cohort size10–14
Funding5 years
Stipend$42,000
Avg time-to-degree5.4 years
Completion (8-yr)86%
Avg pubs at defense3.1

Coursework

Students typically complete all coursework by the end of year two. The minimum is 24 graduate credits beyond the bachelor's, including the EAMS Graduate Seminar in every full-time semester and at least one course in scientific communication.

Qualifying examinations

Two-part qualifier in the second year:

  1. Written exam — an 8-hour open-book exam on the candidate's chosen area, set by the area faculty
  2. Oral defense of research proposal — the candidate presents a 25-page research proposal to their four-person committee and defends it in a 2-hour closed exam

Students who pass both components advance to candidacy and become eligible for the doctoral tuition rate.

Dissertation

The dissertation is normally three to five research chapters, two or three of which should be at least submitted (and ideally published) at the time of defense. The final defense is public, with a private oral exam by the committee immediately afterward.

Typical time-to-degree

The five-year mean reflects field-intensive work in most subdisciplines — multi-year cruise schedules in marine sciences, multiple field seasons for surface-process and glaciology students. Atmospheric chemistry and modeling students typically finish in 4.5 years.

Combined pathway

5-Year combined BS/MS

BS → MS in the same area 5 years · 150 credits

A pathway for strong undergraduates to earn both degrees in five academic years. Students apply during the spring of their junior year; admitted students may double-count up to 12 graduate credits toward both degrees.

Eligibility

  • Brennan undergraduate in the BS Atmospheric, BS Marine, or (with departmental approval) BA Earth Sciences program
  • GPA of 3.4 or higher in the major
  • Endorsement from a prospective master's advisor
  • Completion of at least 2 graduate-level courses by the end of senior year

Funding

5th-year tuition is reduced 40% from the standard graduate rate. Students typically receive a TA appointment in the 5th-year fall and complete a one-semester thesis in the spring. Pathway students are eligible for the same internal fellowships as standard MS students.

Minors & certificates

Minors and certificates

EAMS offers five undergraduate minors and two graduate certificates. Minors require 5–6 courses (20–24 credits) and are open to all Brennan undergraduates. Certificates require 4 graduate courses and are open to currently enrolled graduate students from any department.

Undergraduate minors

  • Minor in Earth Sciences — 5 courses including EAMS 1010 and at least two 3000-level courses
  • Minor in Atmospheric Sciences — 5 courses including EAMS 1110, EAMS 2410, and EAMS 2420
  • Minor in Marine Sciences — 5 courses including EAMS 1210 and two of the 2300-level oceanography sequence
  • Minor in Climate Studies — 6 courses combining science (EAMS 3310) with social-science perspectives on climate
  • Minor in Geospatial Analysis — 5 courses including EAMS 3510 Introduction to GIS

Graduate certificates

  • Graduate Certificate in Environmental Data Science — 4 graduate courses from the Pro MS core; open to graduate students from any Brennan program
  • Graduate Certificate in Coastal Resilience — 4 courses including EAMS 5220 Coastal Adaptation Science & Policy and an applied capstone with a partner municipality
Advising: Minors are advised by Lecturer Soo-Yeon Park (M-202); graduate certificates by Prof. Marta Novak (M-414). Drop-in advising hours are listed on the faculty directory.
